summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting shortly after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. She has a complex history including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube placement due to a previous GJ anastomotic ulcer. She remained on G-tube feeds throughout and was treated with IV fluids, anti-emetics, and continued proton-pump inhibition with lansoprazole. Sucralfate was added for gastric protection. Her symptoms improved over two days, and labs remained normal. The GI team evaluated her and will arrange an outpatient endoscopy to further investigate the cause of her abdominal pain. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue medications, avoid oral intake, and follow up with both the weight loss surgery clinic and GI.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
